sentences.text: 1 The petition filed by the applicant/ petitioner under Section 16 of the Telegraphic Act with a prayer to direct the respondent - Power Grid Corporation of India Limited to pay compensation for all damages as per Section 10(d) of Telegraphic Act.

entities.text: Power Grid Corporation of India Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: .2. The case of the applicant/ petitioner in nutshell is that she is the owner of the schedule agricultural property bearing Sy. No. 24 measuring 2 acres situated at Thippur village, Kengeri Hobli, Bangaluru South Taluka.

The respondent who is the implementing agency of the power grid in the country has formulated a scheme to install a power line i.e., construction of 400 KV Nelamangala - Somanahalli Double Circuit line and the said line is passing through the schedule land.
The petitioner claims that one tower has been put up in the land of petitioner measuring 1200 Square feet.

Thereafter, the respondent has paid the compensation only for removal of trees and determined the compensation in respect of passing of L.A.C. No.77/2012 power transmission lines as well as dispossessing of the petitioner from the portion of the land.

Accordingly claimed that huge loss has been caused to the petitioner and the petitioner is unable to raise any garden crops like coconut, teak etc., Accordingly prayed for compensation.
.3.
In this case, though the respondent served with the notice not chosen to appear before the Court and hence, the respondent has been placed exparte.

.4. The applicant / petitioner is examined herself as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11.
.5.

On the basis of the above, the point for consideration is that:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation for damages as claimed in the petition as per Section 10(d) of the Telegraphic Act?"
.6.
Heard the arguments, the petitioner filed written arguments.

Perused the materials on record, on L.A.C. No.77/2012 that basis, my finding on the above point is in the negative, for the following:
REASONS .7. POINT:

The definite case of the petitioner is that the respondent has put up a electricity tower in the petitioner's property bearing Sy. No. 24 situated at Thippuru village, Kengeri Hobli, Bangaluru South Taluka to the extent of 1200 Square feet.
It is also undisputed and admitted fact that the respondent has paid the compensation in respect of the trees found in the said extent of property.

In this case,
the petitioner also produced the valuation statement for trees or crop compensation at Ex.P.8 and the said statement is dated 15.03.2011.
As per the said document, the petitioner has received Rs. 58,611/- as compensation.
.8. In this case, the petitioner in order to show her ownership over the property, produced a grant certificate at Ex.P.1, Index of lands, record of rights, RTC as per Ex.P.2 to Ex.P.6.

All these documents certainly shows that the petitioner is the owner of the property bearing Sy. No. 24 L.A.C.
No.77/2012 measuring 2 acres of land.

The petitioner produced the notice issued by the respondent at Ex.P.7 and as per the said document/notice, 7 trees are found in the property of petitioner, valued Venkatalakshmamma vs Power Grid Corporation Of India Ltd on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101195828/
2 the compensation and the respondent has paid the compensation for said trees.

sentences.text: .9. It is the definite case of the petitioner that in view of installation of tower and drawing of electricity transmission lines, she is unable to cultivate her land but what is the extent of property that cannot be cultivated by the petitioner in view of drawing of power transmission line as well as installation from the tower is without any explanation.
No document placed by the petitioner to show the extent of property that has been used by the respondent to draw the power transmission line as well as installation / erecting power tower.
There is no material on record to show that the entire property of the petitioner cannot be cultivated in view of drawing power transmission line as well as erection of power transmission tower.

In the absence of any such material on record,
certainly it is not possible for the Court to determine or assess the compensation.
Infact there is no L.A.C. No.77/2012 material on record to show that the power transmission tower has been installed or erected in the property of applicant/ petitioner.

The documents produced by the petitioner at Ex.P.7 and Ex.P.8 only shows that the power transmission lines have been drawn over the property of petitioner and to draw the said power transmission lines, the respondent has removed 7 coconut trees.
Apart from that there is no material whatsoever on record to show that the property of the petitioner has been used by the respondent to draw power transmission lines.
Therefore, it appears that the respondent has awarded proper compensation for removal of 7 coconut trees.
.10. Apart from that what is the value of property of the petitioner in the year 2010 is also without any explanation.
In the absence of any such material before the Court, it is impossible for the Court to determine the compensation.
The case of the petitioner lacks with the identification of property that has been alleged to be used by the respondent or the land rendered useless for the petitioner in view of drawing of line.
Mere production of title deeds and photographs will not L.A.C. No.77/2012 come to the aid of the respondent to determine the compensation.

In view of the aforesaid facts, it is clear that the petitioner/ applicant has miserably failed to make out any grounds to receive the compensation for damages as claimed in the petition as per Section 10(d) of the Telegraphic Act.
Hence, I answer the above point in the negative.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the applicant / petitioner under Section 16 of the Telegraphic Act is hereby dismissed.

(Dictated to the Stenographer Grade-I,
transcribed by her, revised by me and after corrections, pronounced in open Court on this the 3rd day of May, 2025.)
(Padma Prasad) II Addl. City Civil and Sessions Judge, & Spl. Judge, Bangalore .
